author_checkpoint_requirements.confirmation_statement: The author approves the selected combined thesis, the single working title, claims XC1-XC7 with their evidence classes and limitations, the language rules, the legacy claim dispositions, and the contribution boundary bound by this decision-record SHA-256.

claim_evidence_map.denominator_semantics: The evidence is stratified by method over 324 fixed opportunities; methods, frames, branches, and contracts are not experimental replicates.
claim_evidence_map.permitted_claim: Across the two principal scans, operational observability and gap attribution differed between the local Gaussian and native ViPErLEED contracts; failure interpretation was therefore measurement-contract dependent.
claim_evidence_map.required_limitation: This is a comparison of two operational pathways on the same acquisitions, not evidence that either pathway supplies physical-visibility or spot-identity ground truth.

claim_evidence_map.denominator_semantics: Report the four counts separately for each method out of 324 fixed opportunities; do not pool the 1,620 method-opportunity rows as independent observations.
claim_evidence_map.permitted_claim: All 324 opportunities per method were retained, and every method contained more ViPErLEED-only than Gaussian-only observations under the frozen contracts.
claim_evidence_map.required_limitation: The asymmetry is contract-defined and descriptive; it is not a method ranking or a statement that all ViPErLEED-only states are physically visible spots.

claim_evidence_map.denominator_semantics: Gaussian gaps are method-specific; native gaps are beam-specific. The 121 comparison components are descriptive overlap components formed separately within method, scan, and branch.
frozen_anchors: 3/3 shared components have exact boundary agreement
claim_evidence_map.permitted_claim: Bounded gap events were strongly contract-specific: most comparison components contained only Gaussian gaps, while only three components were shared and all three shared exact boundaries.
claim_evidence_map.required_limitation: Neither contract-specific gap is a physical-disappearance claim or a confirmed estimator-independent I(V) visibility gap.

claim_evidence_map.denominator_semantics: The denominator for classification is the 124 accepted Gaussian out-of-branch events, not all opportunities and not the fixed reference-visible set.
frozen_anchors: 25 Unresolved cross-contract outcomes without a direct native observation
claim_evidence_map.permitted_claim: Accepted out-of-branch continuations were not one failure class: native evidence separated branch-model disagreement from Cross-contract target inconsistency and classified events without a direct native observation as Unresolved cross-contract outcomes.
claim_evidence_map.required_limitation: Cross-contract target inconsistency is compatible with possible false persistence but does not prove an identity switch; Unresolved cross-contract outcomes support neither interpretation.

claim_evidence_map.denominator_semantics: The denominator is 121 overlap-connected components, nested within method, scan, and branch; exits are not independent replicates.
frozen_anchors: Both contracts observe at 118/121 component exits
The three non-joint exits remain explicit
claim_evidence_map.permitted_claim: Both contracts returned a direct observation at the first frame after 118 of 121 bounded comparison components.
claim_evidence_map.required_limitation: Call this joint observation at component exit, or contract-specific recovery where appropriate; do not call it proven recovery of physical spot identity.

claim_evidence_map.denominator_semantics: Branch-consistent measurement coverage uses the fixed 221 reference-visible opportunities per method; the all-frame out-of-branch fraction instead uses 206-272 accepted Gaussian fits depending on method.
claim_evidence_map.permitted_claim: Fixed-set branch-consistent measurement coverage and conditional out-of-branch fractions answer different questions and remained separately denominator-bound.
claim_evidence_map.required_limitation: Do not combine these quantities into a generic coverage score or use them to declare a universal best method.

claim_evidence_map.denominator_semantics: All nine predeclared threshold/tolerance combinations and all five method strata are reported, for 45 method-variant rows; no variant is selected.
frozen_anchors: Measurability counts are stable across all 9 variants
Positional tolerance reallocates some direct events between branch-model disagreement and Cross-contract target inconsistency
Unresolved cross-contract outcome counts remain fixed within method
claim_evidence_map.permitted_claim: The measurement-contract observability conclusion was stable over the limited predeclared sensitivity grid, while the split between two direct-event interpretations remained tolerance dependent.
claim_evidence_map.required_limitation: The grid is a bounded robustness check, not parameter optimization, a complete capture-basin analysis, or support for selecting a favorable method ranking.

contribution_boundary.contribution: A cross-contract, denominator-aware assessment of failure semantics in LEED spot-tracking measurement chains.
contribution_boundary.easy_leed_role: EasyLEED is a prior physics-informed LEED-domain tracking baseline evaluated within the frozen comparison; this work does not claim to invent LEED spot tracking or radial scaling.
contribution_boundary.viperleed_role: ViPErLEED supplies a prior indexed whole-pattern native measurement pathway; this work does not claim to invent aperture measurement, native beam indexing, or I(V) extraction.

language_rules.permitted: Use Gaussian-contract gap or ViPEr-native visibility gap and state the contract and bounded-run definition.
language_rules.prohibited: Do not use physical disappearance, true I(V) gap, occlusion, or estimator-independent visibility without separate evidence.

language_rules.permitted: Use contract-specific recovery or both contracts observe at the comparison-component exit, with the event denominator.
language_rules.prohibited: Do not state that physical spot identity was recovered or that each frame is an independent recovery trial.

language_rules.permitted: Use Cross-contract target inconsistency for an accepted continuation more than the frozen tolerance from a direct mapped native target.
language_rules.prohibited: Do not call the event a proven identity switch, tracking error, or native ground-truth failure.

language_rules.permitted: Use no accepted measurement under the named contract. Use abstention only when a method-specific output explicitly records an abstaining state.
language_rules.prohibited: Do not infer deliberate tracker abstention from Gaussian non-measurability, native non-detectability, or a rejected fit alone.

language_rules.permitted: State that Cross-contract target inconsistency is compatible with possible false persistence and requires qualification by the non-ground-truth boundary.
language_rules.prohibited: Do not label branch-model disagreement or Unresolved cross-contract outcomes as false persistence, and do not present possible false persistence as a proven identity switch.

legacy_claim_dispositions.reason: Common-Gaussian suppression of proposal differences is local-contract evidence and cannot support the selected cross-contract thesis. It may remain clearly labeled methodological background.
The Cu positive-control endpoint uses the local Gaussian pathway and a different acquisition regime. It is outside the focused principal-scan claim set.

The prior Gaussian-only stress-test claim cannot remain the cross-contract headline. Replace it with XC1-XC6 so observability, gaps, recovery, and continuation semantics are explicitly contract-specific.

Conditional pair-distance residual similarity depends only on the local Gaussian contract and does not answer the new cross-contract research question. It may remain labeled supporting context outside headline claims.
The SAM2 memory mechanism result uses the local Gaussian pathway only and is not evidence for the selected cross-contract thesis.

The old compatibility claim passes both methods through one Gaussian endpoint. The new principal comparison deliberately preserves ViPErLEED native outputs and must not imply downstream-contract equivalence.
The analytical pairwise-geometry statement remains a valid limitation, but it is not a result claim for the focused cross-contract manuscript.
The temperature-indexed Cu endpoint is local-Gaussian evidence from a different regime and does not support the selected cross-contract thesis.
The saved-proposal missingness diagnostic is specific to the local Gaussian amplitude gate and must not be generalized to native detectability or cross-contract observability.
Any identity-switch, physical-disappearance, false-persistence, or generic visibility claim based on the local Gaussian contract alone exceeds the frozen scientific boundary.

justification: Every method has more ViPErLEED-only than Gaussian-only observations, so observability is not stable across contracts.
The two contracts produce 114 versus 2 bounded gaps, and only 3 of 121 method-stratified comparison components are shared.

The 124 accepted out-of-branch continuations divide into branch-model disagreement, Cross-contract target inconsistency, and Unresolved cross-contract outcomes, so continuity alone cannot determine consistency.
The limited predeclared sensitivity preserves measurability counts but changes some direct-event interpretations, supporting the combined thesis with an explicit tolerance boundary.

rejected_alternatives.reason: It omits the large contract dependence in direct observability and bounded gap definitions.
It omits the scientifically important split of accepted continuous outputs into agreement, Cross-contract target inconsistency, and Unresolved cross-contract outcomes.

thesis_decision.statement: In the tested principal energy scans, LEED spot observability and the interpretation of continuous tracker output depend on the measurement contract: a continuation can remain measurable yet disagree with the predeclared radial branch, agree with the mapped indexed native target, meet the definition of Cross-contract target inconsistency, or remain an Unresolved cross-contract outcome. Robustness therefore requires cross-contract, denominator-aware assessment of both continuity and physical consistency.

working_title: Continuity is not consistency: Cross-contract observability in LEED spot measurement chains
